question: How many loose or watery stools in a day is generally used to define diarrhoea?

options.A: Seven or more mucous stools per day
options.B: Five or more solid stools per day
options.C: Three or more loose stools per day
options.D: One or two hard stools per day

explanation: Passing three or more loose or watery bowel movements within 24 hours is the standard clinical sign that someone has diarrhoea. You've got this! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h1)

question: When does diarrhoea officially change from being acute to chronic based on how long it lasts?

options.A: Chronic diarrhoea lasts longer than four weeks
options.B: Chronic diarrhoea lasts strictly seven to ten days
options.C: Chronic diarrhoea lasts less than forty-eight hours
options.D: Chronic diarrhoea lasts between three and five days

explanation: Think of it this way: short-term (acute) bugs clear up fast, but if diarrhoea hangs around for longer than four weeks, it's classed as chronic and needs a deeper look. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h1)

question: What main process causes osmotic diarrhoea?

options.A: Rapid muscle contractions moving food too fast to digest
options.B: Unabsorbed particles staying in the gut and drawing water in
options.C: Bacterial toxins directly forcing salt and water secretion
options.D: Bleeding ulcers leaking protein and blood into the bowel

explanation: Osmotic means pulling water! When certain substances aren't absorbed in your gut, they act like a magnet, drawing water right along with them into your stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which type of diarrhoea happens when inflammation causes blood, pus, and mucus to leak into the bowel?
explanation: When the gut lining gets inflamed and 'weeps' fluid, blood, or mucus—like in a bad infection or IBD—we call it exudative diarrhoea. Great nursing vocabulary to keep in your toolkit! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic sign that a patient with diarrhoea is starting to get dehydrated?

options.A: Swelling in both lower legs and ankles
options.B: Dry mucous membranes and poor skin turgor
options.D: Increased blood pressure and flushed skin

explanation: When body fluid drops, tissues lose their bounce and moisture. Look out for a sticky dry mouth and skin that takes a moment to snap back when pinched! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h3)

question: A patient with severe diarrhoea complains of dizziness when standing up quickly. What does this finding suggest?

options.A: An acute blockage in the large intestine
options.B: Significant reduction in circulating blood volume
options.C: A sudden spike in systemic blood pressure

explanation: Orthostatic dizziness indicates postural hypotension caused by volume depletion from excessive fluid loss through the gastrointestinal tract. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why would a doctor order a stool culture for a patient with ongoing diarrhoea?

options.A: To isolate and identify specific bacterial or parasitic pathogens
options.B: To determine the patient's exact blood glucose level
options.C: To check for hidden microscopic blood in the stool
options.D: To measure the exact amount of daily fluid loss

explanation: A stool culture lets the lab grow whatever germs are hiding in the sample so the team knows exactly which bacteria or parasite is causing the trouble. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which blood tests are most vital for tracking complications in a patient with severe, ongoing watery stools?

options.A: Liver enzyme panel and lipid profile
options.B: Serum electrolytes and renal function tests
options.C: Fast blood glucose and glycosylated hemoglobin
options.D: Cardiac troponin levels and clotting times

explanation: Diarrhoea washes away key electrolytes like sodium and potassium, and can stress the kidneys. Checking electrolytes and kidney function helps us catch imbalances early! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why should anti-diarrhoea drugs that slow down the gut be avoided in certain bacterial infections?

options.A: They immediately destroy all beneficial gut bacteria
options.B: They permanently stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.C: They cause severe spikes in systemic blood pressure
options.D: Trapping toxins inside the bowel can worsen the illness

explanation: If a patient has a nasty bacterial infection, their body needs to flush the germs out. Slowing down the gut traps those bad toxins inside, which can make them much sicker. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the main job of a medication like loperamide?

options.A: Coating the stomach lining to prevent acid reflux
options.B: Stimulating water absorption by increasing salt intake
options.C: Killing all parasites living in the large intestine
options.D: Slowing down intestinal motility to reduce stool frequency

explanation: Loperamide calms down the bowel muscles (peristalsis) so a patient isn't running to the toilet quite as often. Simple and effective when used correctly! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why do oral rehydration solutions (ORS) mix both salt (sodium) and sugar (glucose) together?

options.A: Sodium prevents the sugar from causing high blood pressure
options.B: Sugar masks the unpleasant salty taste of the solution
options.C: Glucose gives the patient immediate energy to walk around
options.D: Glucose helps transport sodium and water across the intestinal wall

explanation: It's a brilliant biological team-up! Glucose acts like a VIP ticket, helping the intestines pull sodium—and water right along with it—back into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h6)

question: A patient with acute diarrhoea has sore, red skin around their bottom. What is the best immediate nursing step?

options.A: Instruct the patient to avoid washing the area until stools stop
options.B: Gently clean the area, pat dry, and apply a barrier cream
options.C: Place a tight-fitting dressing over the skin to block moisture
options.D: Apply an alcohol-based wipe to disinfect the raw skin thoroughly

explanation: Frequent watery stools are very irritating to the skin. Keeping the area clean, dry, and protected with a good barrier cream is a nursing lifesaver for comfort and skin integrity. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which acid-base imbalance is most likely to happen during severe, long-lasting diarrhoea?

options.A: Respiratory alkalosis from breathing in too much oxygen
options.B: Metabolic acidosis from losing bicarbonate in the stool
options.C: Respiratory acidosis from slowing down breathing rates
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis from retaining too much stomach acid

explanation: Our lower gut secretions are packed with bicarbonate (our body's natural buffer). Losing loads of these fluids means we lose our buffer, leading to metabolic acidosis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the best dietary advice for a patient recovering from a bout of diarrhoea?

options.A: Gradually introduce bland foods and avoid fatty or spicy items
options.B: Immediately return to eating high-fiber raw vegetables and nuts
options.C: Avoid eating all foods completely for at least one full week
options.D: Consume large amounts of whole milk and dairy products daily

explanation: When the gut is healing, it needs an easy time. Bland foods are gentle, whereas fats, spices, and heavy dairy can stir things right back up again. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h7)
